title: SLO contract negotiation and runtime budget rebalancing playbook
author: Anika Patel
content:
-----

Overview

This playbook codifies a single operational workflow for negotiating service-level objective (SLO) contracts between product owners and platform/infra teams and for performing safe "runtime budget rebalancing" when transient or sustained capacity constraints require reallocation of performance headroom across services.

Goals

- Provide a standardized negotiation template for new SLO requests (new routes, new customers, dedicated/dedicated-like tenants).
- Define a guarded runtime procedure to rebalance latency/cost budgets across dependent services while preserving critical safety and degradation contracts.
- Surface observable signals, ownership, and rollback criteria so actions are reversible and auditable.

Scope and assumptions

- Applies to Redwood-hosted API services and Dedicated runtime pools. Private on-premise deployments should follow the same pattern but may require customer-authorized steps (see related_pages).
- Assumes metric instrumentation described below is present and dashboards exist in Grafana/Tempo.
- Does not replace longer-term capacity planning; rebalancing is an operational mitigation.

When to use this playbook

- On-call triggers where end-to-end 95th/99th latency SLOs are slipping and root cause points to cross-service resource contention.
- Predictable transient spikes (e.g., deploy windows, third-party cascade) where pre-negotiated temporary budget shifts reduce incident impact.
- Customer SLA negotiation when a tenant requests a higher throughput/latency commitment that requires dedicated runtime budget.

SLO negotiation template (for product <> infra)

1) Request fields (product owner provides):
   - Service name: (eg. payment-router)
   - Route(s): (eg. /v1/payments/submit)
   - Customer/tenant: internal | external (tenant-id)
   - Desired SLO: P95 latency < 120ms, error-rate < 0.5% (30d lookback)
   - Expected QPS and burst profile: steady 50 qps, burst to 600 qps (2m)
   - Cost preference: prioritize latency | prioritize cost | balanced
   - Canary / rollout plan: percent steps, duration

2) Platform response (infra/platform provides):
   - Feasibility assessment: required GPU/CPU/replica delta, model variant recommendations, quantization impacts
   - Suggested constraints: max burst throttling, admission policy tags, recommended cache-affinity
   - Expected incremental monthly cost estimate and any reservations needed (Dedicated pool commit)
   - Negotiated fallback contract: degraded latency tiers and functional constraints (what features may be disabled under degradation)

3) Signoff criteria
   - Product owner acceptance and stakeholder reviewers (security, SRE, billing)
   - Automated integration tests and perf canary passing in staging with traffic replay
   - ADR reference if the request introduces new runtime controls

Runtime budget rebalancing: principles

- Conservatism: prefer small, incremental shifts with automated verification gates.
- Causality: perform only when telemetry/trace evidence indicates contention crossing service boundaries.
- Short-lived defaults: any emergency reallocation must carry an expiration (TTL) and automated reversion unless extended with manual approval.
- Observability-first: every rebalancing operation must create an audit event and an incident annotation linking action to metrics/dashboards.

Signals and thresholds (examples)

- Key metrics (Prometheus names):
  - http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="edge-proxy",quantile="0.95"}
  - runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio{pool="shared-kv"}
  - gpu_utilization_percent{node_pool="dedicated-1"}
  - inference_tail_latency_ms{model_variant="rwd-v1-small",percentile="99"}
  - request_queue_length{service="runtime-worker"}

- Alert thresholds (baseline):
  - E2E P95 latency increase > 25% above rolling 24h baseline for 5m -> paged to SRE.
  - GPU utilization > 92% sustained for 10m with inference_tail_latency_ms P99 > 800ms -> investigate spillover.
  - Runtime request_queue_length > 1000 for > 3m -> consider admission control.

Guarded rebalancing actions (ordered, smallest blast radius first)

1) Prefix caching warm-up and KV prefetch
   - Owner: runtime-performance
   - Steps:
     a) Trigger an on-demand KV prefetch job for high-frequency keys (CLI: redwood runtime prefetch --service payment-router --keys recent-keys.json).
     b) Monitor cache_hit_ratio for 10 minutes; revert if miss ratio worsens.

2) Dynamic batching window tightening
   - Owner: serving-runtime
   - Steps:
     a) Reduce batching latency target from 30ms -> 15ms for affected pool via runtime-config API.
     b) Verify per-token cost delta and P95 latency within negotiated TTL.
   - YAML example (runtime-config):
     runtime_pool: dedicated-1
     batching:
       target_latency_ms: "15"
       max_batch_size: "64"

3) Route-level admission control and hinting
   - Owner: api-gateway
   - Steps:
     a) Apply temporary admission policy: throttle non-critical routes, preserve critical tenant tags.
     b) Set header hint: x-rw-priority: high|normal|low to guide request shaping.
   - CLI example:
     redwood gateway policy apply --name temp-degrade-2027-01-15 --policy-file policy.yaml

4) Variant downgrade fallback
   - Owner: model-onboarding
   - Steps:
     a) Promote a lower-cost model variant (rwd-v1-small-quant) for non-critical tenants using feature-flagged rollout of 10% -> 50% -> 100%.
     b) Monitor semantic quality evals (prompt-set subset) for drift; if degradation exceeds 5% regressions, rollback.

5) Cross-pool weight reallocation (most invasive)
   - Owner: platform-capacity
   - Steps:
     a) Execute rebalancing only after approval from SRE lead and product owner. Create RFC ticket.
     b) Use orchestration API to shift N% of capacity from pool A -> pool B with a rate limit of 5%/minute.
     c) Annotate the change with TTL and approval metadata. Example API call:
        curl -X POST https://platform-api.internal/v1/pools/rebalance \
          -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLATFORM_TOKEN" \
          -d '{"from_pool":"shared-burst","to_pool":"dedicated-1","percent":10,"ttl_minutes":60,"approved_by":"anika.patel"}'
     d) Monitor end-to-end SLOs and the donor pool for collateral impact. Auto-revert if donor pool P95 exceeds 110% of baseline.

Audit, TTLs and automatic reversion

- Every rebalancing action must set TTL metadata; defaults:
  - Prefix cache and batching tweaks: TTL = 30 minutes
  - Admission policies: TTL = 60 minutes
  - Variant downgrade: TTL = 120 minutes with mandatory quality check after 15 minutes
  - Pool reallocation: TTL = 60 minutes, require manual extension

- Reversion tests:
  - Automated healthcheck job runs TTL/2 and TTL-5m to assert observed metrics against rollback criteria.
  - If healthchecks fail, system reverts the change and pages SRE with incident summary.

Communication and incident annotations

- Create an incident in PagerDuty and Slack #inc-ops channel with the action bundle including links to dashboards and traces.
- Add the following annotation fields to incident ticket: action_id, action_type, owner, start_ts, ttl, expected_improvement, revert_criteria.

Post-action review and required artifacts

1) Short postmortem (if action was invoked during a page) within 48 hours. Include:
   - Timeline of rebalancing actions
   - Metrics before/during/after
   - Root cause analysis and whether rebalancing masked or exposed the root cause
   - Follow-up actions (capacity reservations, ADRs, customer communication)

2) Add/update an ADR when:
   - The rebalancing introduces a persistent contract change (example: permanent priority tiers for a tenant)
   - New runtime knobs or policies are added that affect backward compatibility

Example ADR summary (required fields)

- Title: ADR - Temporary runtime budget reallocation protocol
- Decision: Adopt the guarded, TTL-based reallocation protocol with audit annotations and automated reversion.
- Consequences: Requires instrumentation and incident tooling changes; small operational overhead but reduces incident blast radius.

Safe playbook checklist (pre-action)

- [ ] Incident paged and triaged
- [ ] Verify telemetry and service ownership
- [ ] Confirm SLOs that will be impacted and notify stakeholders
- [ ] Create RFC/approval in ticket system if action will exceed minor threshold (pool reallocation)

Emergency timeline template (communication)

- 0–10m: Triage and initial actions (cache prefetch, batching tweak)
- 10–30m: Admission control + variant fallbacks if needed
- 30–90m: Pool weight reallocation (if approved) and monitoring
- 90m+: Reversion or extension with documented approvals
